_comment: Data processing manifest: normalizes three input files in different formats (CSV, XML, TSV) into a consistent JSON structure. Each task uses jq to validate the output after writing it. allowed_tools includes Bash restricted to jq so the agent can reshape data without arbitrary shell access.

tasks.name: normalize-csv-contacts
tasks.prompt: Read the file raw/contacts.csv. Parse every row and normalize the data into a JSON array where each object has exactly these fields: { "id": string, "full_name": string, "email": string, "phone": string, "country": string }. Apply these normalizations: trim whitespace from all values, convert phone numbers to E.164 format (+CC-number), lowercase all email addresses, leave missing optional fields as empty string. Write the result to normalized/contacts.json. Then run `jq 'map(has("id", "full_name", "email", "phone", "country"))' normalized/contacts.json` to confirm every record has all required fields.

tasks.name: normalize-xml-inventory
tasks.prompt: Read the file raw/inventory.xml. Parse the XML and normalize the data into a JSON array where each object has exactly these fields: { "sku": string, "name": string, "category": string, "quantity": number, "unit_price_usd": number }. Apply these normalizations: strip any currency symbols from prices, convert quantity to integer, lowercase category names. Write the result to normalized/inventory.json. Then run `jq 'map(select(.unit_price_usd < 0)) | length' normalized/inventory.json` to verify there are no negative prices.

tasks.name: normalize-tsv-survey
tasks.prompt: Read the file raw/survey-responses.tsv. Parse every tab-separated row and normalize the data into a JSON array where each object has exactly these fields: { "respondent_id": string, "age_group": string, "region": string, "score": number, "comments": string }. Apply these normalizations: trim whitespace, convert score to a number between 0 and 100 (scale if necessary), replace newlines in comments with a space. Write the result to normalized/survey-responses.json. Then run `jq '[.[] | select(.score > 100 or .score < 0)] | length' normalized/survey-responses.json` to verify all scores are in range.
